Prepare a cohort survey design

Source: R/design.R
nis_design.Rd

Build a survey design from the annual sample and the declared cohort. Use the result with srvyr, survey, and gtsummary.

Usage

nis_design(
  .data,
  cohort,
  keep,
  annualize = FALSE,
  dollars = NULL,
  charges = "TOTCHG"
)

Arguments

.data

Lazy DuckDB query or data frame. Existing dplyr groups and rowwise grouping are removed before evaluating cohort; aggregate cohort expressions therefore use the full input, not individual input groups.

cohort

Logical data-masked cohort expression. Missing values are counted and treated as outside the cohort. Only valid-design discharges are counted. Untyped SQL NULL values are accepted as missing logical values. Lazy columns are validated using their SQL type; numeric and character columns are rejected even when all missing.

keep

Tidyselect expression naming analysis columns to collect. Renaming uses the selected source values and labels. Required design fields remain under their original names, as do selected cost inputs when costs are computed. Aliases cannot overwrite these retained fields or computed cost columns. Type predicates inspect actual columns locally and a zero-row schema for lazy queries; predicates depending on row values are therefore not portable across backends.

annualize

Divide every discharge weight by the number of years with valid design records. Each partial year counts as one year.

dollars

Reference dollar year for adjusted charges and costs. To set it, keep the charge field and CCR_NIS.

charges

Name of the charge field. Defaults to "TOTCHG". Choose the field for the years analyzed. See Years and coding eras.

Value

A filtered srvyr::tbl_svy survey design. The analysis data contains the required design fields, the columns selected by keep, and any computed cost columns. nis_label() keeps binary indicators logical and converts known multi-level codes to factors. Use stats::weights() for the survey weights.

Details

Hospital and stratum identifiers include the year. Hospital-years without eligible discharges contribute zero to the domain calculation. Filter the returned design to estimate within a smaller domain. For a dataset saved with nis_write_cohort(), omit cohort.

Invalid design fields

The design excludes discharges with missing, non-finite, or nonpositive YEAR, HOSP_NIS, NIS_STRATUM, or DISCWT. Inspect the excluded counts by field and year with nis_design_report().

Adjusted charges and costs

Keeping both the charge field and CCR_NIS adds charges_adj and cost_adj. The default dollar year is the latest included design year. Set dollars to use another reference year.

See also

Make tables and fit survey models, Make tables and fit survey models.

Other survey-design: nis_design_report(), nis_reweight(), nis_survey()

Examples

nis <- nis_open(nis_example(years = 2019:2020)) |>
  nis_flag_dx(heart_failure = "I50")
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/Rtmpq6Jh4y/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/Rtmpq6Jh4y/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
design <- nis_design(
  nis,
  cohort = heart_failure & AGE >= 50,
  keep = c(AGE, FEMALE, TOTCHG, CCR_NIS),
  dollars = 2024
)
#> Preparing the cohort survey design.
srvyr::summarise(
  design,
  discharges = srvyr::survey_total(),
  mean_age = srvyr::survey_mean(AGE)
)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 4
#>   discharges discharges_se mean_age mean_age_se
#>        <dbl>         <dbl>    <dbl>       <dbl>
#> 1       83.2          11.8     69.7       0.607
